That's fair enough, the game might just not be your kind of thing, which can happen with every game, no matter how praised, different strokes and all that.

But in HR's defense (with regards to your specific points):

Direct combat happens essentially as much as you'll allow it to happen. Or, to put it differently: The maps / missions are essentially sandboxes where you're rather free to pick how your approach, whether that is completely silent, and non-lethal with hand to hand knockouts only, using tranquilizer darts or silenced guns, or going in guns blazing with a shotgun and explosives, or any possible combination of that. All of those approaches are equally valid as far as the game is concerned. One difference (I've always critizised myself) is that the super-pacifist, no-kills, 100% stealth route will net you more XP, but to be fair, most of the stuff you'll spend XP on is skills related to that exact type of approach, so if you, for example, decide to role-play a shotgun-blazing gunslinger, you won't have a lot of need for many of the skills in the game anyway, so it's not like you're completely gimping yourself. That aside, the game really isn't particularly difficult and perfectly playable no matter what approach you take.

With that in mind, the gameplay concepts are very, very similar to the original Deus Ex (down to the map design allowing for that gameplay, even), which is one of the reasons for the praise HR received. So, out of curiosity, have you played the original Deus Ex and did you find to be as uninterested in it as HR? Because if HR is the first DX game you've played and you couldn't get into it, and this really isn't meant to sound cocky or anything, but the series might just not scratch your particular itch, so to speak, I guess?
